closed_r1_p0.closure: K1 resource preflight remains in a unique temporary directory; canonical and attempt remain absent on preflight-only failure, while post-canonical/pre-attempt failure moves canonical to a PID-unique quarantine.
The full exact identity including absolute runner is checked initially, before and after every point, at both final boundaries, and against the initial input manifest.
Runtime monitor latches cgroup OOM state; monitor rc, post-point cgroup, and final cgroup checks are all hard gates.

p0.finding: Python writes the canonical PASS receipt, RUN_COMPLETE, manifest, and seal before the final exact-input and cgroup checks. A postcheck failure leaves a sealed standard-named PASS set plus a later failure marker.
p0.impact: Downstream consumers can admit a failed run by discovering RUN_COMPLETE or the valid seal without interpreting the unsealed later failure marker.
p0.required_repair: Stage all root PASS artifacts until final hard checks pass, then atomically publish; or quarantine all standard PASS artifacts on any post-publication failure.

p1.finding: The atomic attempt directory has two identity members but no inner/outer seal or final rehash.
p1.recommended_repair: Seal the two members before rename and rehash the attempt at final completion.

p1.finding: Plain mv can nest staging under an unexpectedly existing target directory instead of rejecting it.
p1.recommended_repair: Use same-filesystem mv -T or an equivalent target-must-be-absent primitive, then verify members at the canonical attempt root.
